models.summary: Total carbon in a year is living wood plus products. Harvested area is the rate times total area, divided by the cosine of the slope. Living area prints 1 minus a, not 1 minus the rate. Capacity is a fitted curve whose exponent is jammed on the line. The age share prints a broken glyph around the rate. Living carbon sums ages 1 to 100. Harvested carbon sums ages 81 to 100. Product carbon adds the current year, products in use, and landfill. The half-life exponent does not stay on the baseline. Hardwood is 30 years and paper is 2. Landfill is a sum with no decay.
models.computational_cost: Two area lines, two age sums, and one product sum with an unnamed half-life
models.purpose: Turn area, age, and product life into a carbon total.
objectives: Maximize carbon by cutting only trees past the cutting age of 81.

models.section: Dynamic optimization of the harvest rate
models.summary: Each year picks a rate from 0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, and 0.9 percent. The sum of those rates over 100 years is at most 50 percent. Dynamic programming is named. The ideal forest is said to come from random numbers, and the area used is the 2014 Beijing primary forest. The dots are read as a cycle of about 20 years. The maximum is 8.62 times 10 to the 9 kilograms. Because the rate is small, this search does not include a harvesting interval.
models.computational_cost: A discrete rate each year under one sum cap
models.purpose: Choose the annual rates that maximize the carbon total.
objectives: Maximize the year total subject to the rates summing to at most 50 percent.

variables.definition: Year total from the sequestration model, the quantity being maximized

governing_equations.equation_text: The objective maximizes living carbon plus product carbon. The sum of the annual rates over 100 years is at most 50 percent. Each rate is one of 0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, and 0.9 percent.

algorithm.convergence_criteria: The printed maximum is 8.62 times 10 to the 9 kilograms, read as a cycle of about 20 years.

details: The cap and the five rates print. The stage recursion does not.
identifiability_feasibility.analysis: The search is said to omit the harvesting interval because the rate is small.

constraints: Each annual rate is one of the five printed percents.
The hundred-year sum is at most 50 percent.

limitations: The ideal forest is random and the area is Beijing.

models.summary: Value is ecology, society, and economy. Profit is tourism revenue minus forest-product revenue. A metric divides an actual value by the area-wide value and multiplies by 100, and it reuses equation number 19. The score is 0.5816 times ecology plus 0.1095 times society plus 0.3090 times economy. Those three add to 1.0001. The factor table is shifted by a row. An interval returns the area to its pre-cut state and is minus the log of 1 minus the rate, over the log of 1 plus the growth rate. Five programs are printed on shifted rows. Beijing scores 4.0677 and is given program three, 0.06 percent and 30 years. A ten-year lengthening asks for 0.09 percent.
models.computational_cost: One weighted score and one closed interval
